images.title: Only the remainders matter
images.purpose: Shows 17 as 3 groups of 5 with 2 loose and 24 as 4 groups of 5 with 4 loose; the 6 loose dots make one more group and leave 1, so 17 + 24 leaves remainder 1.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two dot clusters side by side, with their loose dots gathered below.
images.exact_structure: Left cluster labelled 17: 3 groups of 5 teal (#0072B2) dots, each group in a thin grey ring, and 2 loose amber (#E69F00) dots. Right cluster labelled 24: 4 groups of 5 teal (#0072B2) dots in thin grey rings, and 4 loose amber (#E69F00) dots. Below, centred, the 6 loose amber dots gathered under the label 2 + 4 = 6: 5 of them inside one thin grey ring and 1 outside it in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) circle labelled remainder 1. Thin grey arrows lead from the loose dots of each cluster down to the gathered group. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The remainder of a sum comes from adding the remainders.
images.description: Shows 17 as 3 groups of 5 with 2 loose and 24 as 4 groups of 5 with 4 loose; the 6 loose dots make one more group and leave 1, so 17 + 24 leaves remainder 1.
images.teaching_notes: The 6 loose dots are the same dots moved down.

image_decisions.why: Grouped dots show why only the leftovers decide the remainder of a sum.
